design.title: One direction per tile: a normalised-prototype cosine head with an additive margin replaces the affine cell classifier, so every survey's picture of a place must point the same way
design.eli5: Until now the model's last step was a big lookup table that could quietly keep three separate 'looks' for every map tile - one per survey photograph it trained on - and a fourth photograph matched none of them. We replace that table with a compass: every map tile gets exactly one direction, and every picture of a place, from whichever survey, is trained to point that way with a safety margin against the neighbouring tiles. This is the same trick face recognition uses to know one person across many photos instead of memorising each photo. If it works, a photograph the model has never seen should still point at the right tile, because that is now the only way the model knows how to point.
design.hypothesis: Ten experiments on this ruler leave the held-out 2024 photograph at 7.5% usable (exp 7, 1.096), with usable never outside 7-14% while the training photographs ranged 17-96% at the same held-out viewpoints: the deployed feature of a place still moves with the survey, and the cell head tolerates that. The exp 9 design-stage probe measured it on the champion's own exported graph (runs/_probe_exp9_wpv.py, three TRAINING captures only): a change of survey moves a member's pooled feature 30% as far as a change of place (within-place variance fraction 0.295), and the SAME member names the same cell for the same place in two training surveys only 28-40% of the time. Three attempts to close that spread were all AUXILIARY terms added beside an affine softmax head and none got a fair test: exp 3's cosine term was satisfied for free by post-ReLU positivity (0.966 at epoch 1), exp 9's standardised variance penalty at weight 10 collapsed training (top1 0.008), exp 10's reconstruction target left the head free to read survey cues beside the canonical ones. The common cause is not the targets but the HEAD: an affine linear classifier (w_c . f + b_c) over an unnormalised feature can raise a sample's margin by growing feature and weight norms instead of by reducing angular spread, so it is content to store a summer, a leaf-off and an early-spring signature of each tile as three directions inside one wide cone (exp 2 did exactly that: 95% usable on each training photograph, 7% on the fourth). This is the problem face recognition solved a decade ago for one identity across many photographs: normalise the feature AND the class prototype so the logit is a pure cosine, scale it by a fixed s, and train with an additive margin (NormFace, Wang et al. 2017; CosFace, Wang et al. 2018). With norms fixed, the ONLY way to lower the loss is angular - pull every photograph of a tile toward that tile's single prototype direction and push the 2,970 prototypes apart - so intra-class compactness across surveys becomes the main objective rather than a side term: it cannot be vacuous (the embedding is batch-normalised before normalisation, so unrelated places sit near cosine 0, not 0.7), it cannot collapse (2,970 prototypes must separate), and it cannot be side-stepped by norm growth. A fourth survey's feature of a place then only has to land inside the compact cap around the prototype it was trained to share with three others, rather than inside one of three memorised directions. The design-stage probe for THIS experiment (runs/_probe_exp11_illum.py) closed the alternative explanation first: no fixed input transform - grey, chromaticity, local contrast normalisation, gradient magnitude, or the Maddern illumination-invariant channel at any alpha - makes the same place more alike across the training surveys than raw RGB (same-place correlation 0.52 for RGB vs 0.32-0.42 for every transform), and deep-shadow state disagrees on only 4-8% of pixels, so the gap is not shadows or colour that a preprocessing step could remove; it has to be closed where the feature is read. The 'Map-cell classifier' stage has never carried changed:true in this era except for exp 7's averaging; this experiment changes how it reads the feature, on both committee members, and leaves trunk, pooling, offset head, committee gate, paired batches and nuisance randomisation untouched. Library L2 rank 1 (cross-survey latent consistency) is what this delivers, by parameterisation instead of by loss.
